correctness.rationale: The normalization b=c=1, a=x with 0<x<2 is exhaustive up to similarity. All median, altitude, semiperimeter and inradius formulas are exact. Rationalization produces a sign-aware three-interval proof; no squaring is used without controlling signs. The outer intervals reduce to an exact factorization over Q(sqrt(3)); the left sign is certified by positive Bernstein coefficients of Q' and Q(4/7)<0, while the right sign follows from exact shifted coefficient positivity and a quadratic discriminant -10. Equality is checked exactly and occurs only at x=1. The bundled checker reconstructs and verifies all algebraic certificates using standard-library rational arithmetic.

originality.rationale: The source paper states the all-triangle conjecture but does not supply this isosceles resolution. published-finding corpus searches for the exact difference inequality, aliases, and isosceles specialization returned no covering finding. The later 2021 full text addresses a different median/bisector/exradius double inequality, the 2017 Monthly result is an upper bound for the median sum alone, and the closely related 2023 Lemma 2 gives a summable m_a-h_a lower bound that is strictly too weak at (a,b,c)=(1/2,1,1). No checked statement implies the present theorem; residual risk is limited to unindexed or differently phrased literature.
residual_risks: Search coverage cannot exclude an unindexed, non-English, or differently phrased earlier proof of the isosceles specialization.
The 2012 source uses 2000 MSC 51M16; the present record maps it directly to the permitted geometry primary class 51M16.

value.rationale: Liu explicitly posed the inequality as a conjectured sharp lower bound and connected it to Blundon's inequality. The isosceles family is the full natural symmetry subclass of triangles, spans every admissible aspect ratio, and contains the sharp equilateral equality case. A complete proof on this subclass is a motivated structural partial resolution rather than an arbitrary numerical slice.
